evals.prompt: My Zed extension in zed-ruff/ is supposed to start Ruff's language server for Python files, but it never starts and Zed.log shows nothing about it. The Rust code builds fine. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: extension.toml uses [language_servers.ruff] (underscore; Zed ignores the hyphenated table) and languages = ["Python"] matching the built-in language name exactly; the checker passes; the reply gives the dev-install steps and marks them not run.

assertions.text: The extension passes the bundled checker without the --registry rules.
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py"; python3 "$t" zed-ruff

assertions.text: extension.toml declares [language_servers.ruff] with languages exactly ["Python"] and no hyphenated table.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import tomllib; m = tomllib.load(open("zed-ruff/extension.toml", "rb")); assert "language-servers" not in m, m; assert m["language_servers"]["ruff"]["languages"] == ["Python"], m["language_servers"]'

assertions: The reply explains both causes: Zed ignores the hyphenated [language-servers] table, and language names must match Zed's language name exactly (Python, not python).
The reply lists the in-editor steps (zed: install dev extension, then check Zed.log or zed --foreground) and marks them as not run unless the transcript shows Zed running.

evals.prompt: Create a Zed extension in zed-just/ that adds justfile support (files named justfile or Justfile, or ending in .just) using the grammar at https://github.com/IndianBoy42/tree-sitter-just. I want syntax highlighting and recipes in the outline. No language server.
evals.expected_output: extension.toml with a [grammars.just] entry pinned to a 40-character commit SHA, languages/just/config.toml (name, grammar, path_suffixes covering justfile, Justfile, and just), highlights.scm and outline.scm using Zed capture names, no Cargo.toml or Rust; both checkers pass.

assertions.text: zed-just/ passes the bundled extension checker (grammar rev is a 40-character SHA, config and query files valid).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py"; python3 "$t" zed-just

assertions.text: The language directory passes the bundled query checker and contains highlights.scm and outline.scm.
assertions.check: l=$(dirname "$(find zed-just/languages -name config.toml | head -n 1)"); test -f "$l/highlights.scm" && test -f "$l/outline.scm" || { echo "missing highlights.scm or outline.scm in $l"; exit 1; }; d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_queries.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_queries.py"; python3 "$t" "$l"

assertions.text: The language config matches justfile, Justfile, and .just files.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import glob, tomllib; c = tomllib.load(open(glob.glob("zed-just/languages/*/config.toml")[0], "rb")); s = set(c.get("path_suffixes", [])); assert {"justfile", "Justfile", "just"} <= s, s'

assertions.text: No Rust crate was added (the extension needs no code).

assertions: The reply states how the grammar commit SHA was obtained (for example git ls-remote) and does not claim the queries were compiled with tree-sitter or tested in Zed unless the transcript shows it.

evals.prompt: I made a Zed theme (night-lang/themes/night.json) and I'd like to ship it inside our existing 'Night Language' extension in night-lang/, which we're about to submit to the Zed extension registry. Some colors are written as CSS names like "tomato" and I used a "foreground" key in the style. Get it ready.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the registry rejects themes mixed with languages and moves the theme to its own extension (for example night-theme/ with extension.toml, LICENSE, and themes/night.json); replaces CSS color names with hex; replaces the foreground style key with text/editor.foreground; night-lang passes check_extension --registry.

assertions.text: night-lang/ passes the bundled checker with --registry (no theme mixed into the language extension).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py"; python3 "$t" night-lang --registry

assertions.text: A separate extension directory with extension.toml ships the theme, and it passes the bundled checker.
assertions.check: e=$(for f in $(find . -path ./.claude -prune -o -path ./night-lang -prune -o -name extension.toml -print); do d=$(dirname "$f"); ls "$d"/themes/*.json >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "$d"; done | head -n 1); test -n "$e" || { echo "no extension with themes/*.json outside night-lang"; exit 1; }; d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-zed-editor-extensions/scripts/check_extension.py"; python3 "$t" "$e"

assertions.text: Every color in the shipped theme is a hex value and no style uses a "foreground" key.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import glob, json, re; ps = [p for p in glob.glob("*/themes/*.json") if not p.startswith("night-lang/")]; assert ps, "no theme outside night-lang"; bad = []; walk = lambda k, v: [walk(k2, v2) for k2, v2 in v.items()] if isinstance(v, dict) else ([walk(k, x) for x in v] if isinstance(v, list) else (bad.append((k, v)) if isinstance(v, str) and k != "font_style" and not re.fullmatch(r"#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}", v) else None)); styles = [t["style"] for p in ps for t in json.load(open(p))["themes"]]; [walk("style", s) for s in styles]; bad += [("foreground", s["foreground"]) for s in styles if "foreground" in s]; assert not bad, bad'

assertions: The reply explains that the Zed extension registry does not accept a theme bundled with a language extension, which is why the theme moved to its own extension.

evals.prompt: On my Mac, `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip2` for my Zed extension fails with error[E0463]: can't find crate for `core`. `rustup target list --installed` already shows wasm32-wasip2 and `which cargo` prints /opt/homebrew/bin/cargo. What's going on and what exactly should I run? Don't change my system yourself; just tell me.
evals.expected_output: Homebrew's Rust shadows rustup on PATH and has no wasm32-wasip2 standard library, so the target that rustup installed is invisible to it. Fix: run rustup's toolchain (~/.cargo/bin first on PATH, or rustup run stable cargo build ...), or remove the Homebrew rust; verify with `rustc --print sysroot` and `which -a cargo`.

assertions.text: The reply points at rustup's toolchain (~/.cargo/bin, rustup run, or a rustup proxy) as the cargo to use.
The run did not install, uninstall, or relink toolchains on the host.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import json, os, re; ev = [json.loads(l) for l in open(os.environ["EVAL_TRANSCRIPT_FILE"]) if l.strip().startswith("{")]; cmds = [c.get("input", {}).get("command", "") for e in ev if e.get("type") == "assistant" for c in (e.get("message") or {}).get("content") or [] if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("type") == "tool_use" and c.get("name") == "Bash"]; bad = [c for c in cmds if re.search(r"brew (install|uninstall|remove|unlink|link)|rustup (target add|toolchain (install|uninstall)|default|self)", c)]; assert not bad, bad'

assertions: The reply explains that the Homebrew cargo/rustc is found first on PATH and has no standard library for wasm32-wasip2, so rustup's installed target does not apply to it.
The reply gives a way to confirm the diagnosis, such as `which -a cargo`, `rustc --print sysroot`, or `rustup which cargo`.

evals.prompt: In Zed, I want Markdown files to soft-wrap at 80 columns and use a tab size of 2. My settings file is zed-config/settings.json. Just my editor settings, please.
evals.expected_output: settings.json gains "languages": {"Markdown": {"soft_wrap": "preferred_line_length" (or "bounded"), "preferred_line_length": 80, "tab_size": 2}} and keeps the existing keys; no extension files.

assertions.text: settings.json has a Markdown language override with a soft_wrap mode that uses the preferred line length, preferred_line_length 80, and tab_size 2, and keeps the theme.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import json, re; t = open("zed-config/settings.json").read(); t = re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", t, flags=re.M); t = re.sub(r",(\s*[}\]])", r"\1", t); s = json.loads(t); md = s["languages"]["Markdown"]; assert md.get("soft_wrap") in ("preferred_line_length", "bounded"), md; assert md.get("preferred_line_length") == 80 and md.get("tab_size") == 2, md; assert s.get("theme") == "One Dark", s'

assertions.text: No extension files (extension.toml, Cargo.toml) were created.
